headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors: Goose’s filesystem/MCP access can ingest and act on ACI outputs by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ACI can emit content through APIs/MCP, and Goose reads the filesystem and uses MCP extensions, so A’s outputs can be fed into B as trusted input. The shared channel is plausible by default, but the profiles do not show a raw web-content parser or clipboard bridge, so medium is the higher justified severity.
conditions: IF ACI output is written into a file or MCP message that Goose consumes without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF Goose treats ACI-generated text as instructions rather than data, prompt hijacking can occur.
mitigations: Add a provenance header to all ACI outputs before Goose reads them.
Require Goose to parse ACI output as structured data only.
Disable automatic ingestion of shared files between the agents.
Use a separate workspace directory for each agent.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing at the orchestrator boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ACI touches CRM, email, calendar, support, and research data and has broad network egress; Goose reads and writes the user filesystem and can use MCP servers. If ACI places sensitive records in shared files or passes them through MCP, Goose can expose them onward. The blast radius includes customer and email data, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF ACI writes CRM or email data into the shared cwd, Goose can read it.
IF Goose forwards shared-file contents to configured model providers or MCP servers, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Move sensitive ACI outputs to a private directory Goose cannot read.
Turn off Goose access to shared workspaces for sensitive runs.
Redact CRM/email fields before handoff.
Review MCP server destinations before enabling them.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs and egress policy.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and Goose can write the filesystem and modify git state while ACI can operate through APIs/MCP and supports multiple instances. If they share a workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide without locking. The profiles show a direct shared-state path via filesystem, so high is justified.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same git checkout, concurrent commits or edits can conflict.
IF ACI and Goose write to the same files without locks, state corruption can occur.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Pause one agent before the other mutates git state.
Use file locks around shared outputs.
Limit Goose to read-only mode during ACI runs.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control and merge arbitration.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ACI can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and Goose can execute shell, modify git, and call MCP tools. If Goose treats ACI output as authoritative, a mistaken or injected ACI result can cascade into real actions or commits. Because downstream action-taking authority exists in Goose and ACI can produce operational outputs, high is appropriate.
conditions: IF Goose consumes ACI output without verification, incorrect facts can trigger actions.
IF ACI output is used to populate commands, emails, or commits, errors propagate downstream.
mitigations: Require human review before Goose executes ACI-derived actions.
Add a verification step that cross-checks ACI outputs against source systems.
Restrict Goose to dry-run mode for ACI-fed tasks.
Log and diff all ACI-derived commands before execution.
requires-engineering: implement typed contracts between ACI and Goose.

E_compliance.rationale: ACI handles CRM, customer support, email, and calendar data, while Goose reads/writes local files and uses third-party model providers and MCP servers. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if regulated customer data is copied into Goose-managed files or sent to external providers. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the higher safe choice.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is copied from ACI into Goose-managed files, retention policies may diverge.
IF Goose sends those files to external model providers, compliance obligations can be breached.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Goose workspaces.
Use a data-classification checklist before handoff.
Disable external provider calls for sensitive runs.
Set short retention on shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: align retention, residency, and DPA controls across both agents.
